Asked whether the current support for visually impaired students in Hong Kong is sufficient, Cheng expressed satisfaction, but noted that different types of visually impaired individuals have their own needs, and hoped that society could achieve greater inclusion. In addition, Cheng shared that the secret to being a top scorer lies in handwritten notes, which help deepen memory, complemented by AI assistance.

Cheng shared that he will stay in Hong Kong to study Politics and Law at the University of Hong Kong. Having been exposed to law-related experiences and opportunities from an early age, he developed an interest in the legal field. He said he "believes the law can bring equality and opportunities," and hopes to become a barrister in the future, using the law to bring legal accessibility to members of the public who lack financial means or are in poorer physical condition.

When asked about his thoughts on the current instability in Hong Kong's political environment, Cheng said his "original intention has remained unchanged." Social and economic instability would "not affect my aspiration to pursue (law)" and he "believes the law can bring opportunities to people." Regarding whether AI will replace legal work, Cheng believes that law requires an understanding of "human nature and worldly affairs," and that AI cannot replace human emotion.

On the journey of growing up, family support is also very important. Cheng's father said, "He (Cheng) is a very hardworking person," believing that Cheng's efforts and the message he conveys can "encourage fellow travellers." Mr Cheng said, "All parents hope their children can grow up healthy." Upon learning of Cheng's eye condition, it also took him a long time to come to terms with reality, but fortunately he received help from organisations such as the Hong Kong Society for the Blind.
